name: Pale Court Thrall
desc: A coerced or enthralled mortal used as disposable muscle.
motives: Obey, isolate the target, flee if the bond breaks
features: **Pack Pressure — Passive:** When another Thrall is within Very Close range of the same target, add +1 to this Thrall’s attack roll (maximum +2).

**Break the Hold — Reaction:** When the Thrall is shown undeniable proof that its master has abandoned it, the PC can make a Presence Roll (11). On a success, remove this Thrall from the conflict without defeating them.

name: Aster Vale Contractor
desc: A well-paid field operative trained to contain unusual incidents without asking moral questions.
motives: Secure evidence, control witnesses, avoid public spectacle
features: **Professional Entry — Passive:** The Contractor has advantage on the first roll made to breach, restrain, or surprise a prepared position.
**Flashbang — Action:** Mark a Stress. A target within Close range makes an Instinct Reaction Roll (12). On a failure, they become **Vulnerable** and mark a Stress; on a success, choose one.

name: Aster Vale Occult Analyst
desc: A field researcher carrying ward readers, predictive models, and too much confidence in procedure.
motives: Measure, identify patterns, keep the team informed
features: **Mark the Variable — Action:** Mark a Stress to study a PC within Far range. Until the Analyst next takes Severe damage, one allied adversary gains +2 Difficulty against that PC’s next action.

**Readout — Reaction:** When a PC uses an obvious supernatural feature, the Analyst may mark a Stress to identify its broad source and tell one allied adversary how to counter it; that adversary gains advantage on its next reaction roll against that feature.

name: Static Wraith
desc: A dead impression riding radio noise, electrical arcs, and screen glow.
motives: Be heard, overload circuits, repeat the moment of death
features: **Ride the Current — Passive:** The Wraith can move between powered devices within Close range without crossing the intervening space.

**Feedback — Reaction:** When a PC uses an electronic device within Close range, the Wraith may mark a Stress to force an Instinct Reaction Roll (12). On a failure, the PC marks a Stress and the device shuts down until repaired or reset.

name: Veil-Burned Stalker
desc: A person whose exposure to a rupture left them half-visible to normal attention and addicted to supernatural proximity.
motives: Follow power, steal occult objects, remain unseen
features: **Peripheral — Passive:** Until the Stalker attacks or speaks directly to the PC, rolls to notice them are at disadvantage unless the PC is specifically searching.
**Steal the Focus — Action:** Spend a Fear. Move the Stalker from Close to Melee range without a roll and make a standard attack. On a success, the PC also loses 1 Hope if they have any.

name: Hexbound Familiar
desc: A small animal, doll, shadow, or object carrying a practitioner’s remote attention.
motives: Observe, carry links, interfere, escape intact
features: **Sympathetic Relay — Passive:** A hidden creator can originate simple Hex effects through the Familiar while it remains within Far range of the target.

**Snatch a Link — Action:** Make an attack roll against a target in Melee. On a success, deal no damage; instead the Familiar steals a small personal object, hair, blood trace, or similar sympathetic link if one is exposed.

name: River Hound
desc: A dog-shaped water spirit built from runoff, river mud, broken glass, and territorial memory.
motives: Drive intruders away, defend water, drag prey toward the river
features: **Flow Around It — Passive:** The Hound can pass through gaps large enough for flowing water.

**Drag Down — Action:** After a successful attack, spend a Fear to force a Strength Reaction Roll (12). On a failure, move the target to Very Close range toward the nearest significant water and make them **Vulnerable** until they regain footing.

name: Memory Leech
desc: A translucent psychic parasite that feeds on recent emotional memory.
motives: Feed, hide inside confusion, avoid direct confrontation
features: **Blank Spot — Reaction:** When the Leech deals damage, the target makes a Knowledge Reaction Roll (12). On a failure, they temporarily lose access to one relevant Experience until the end of the scene.
**Taste the Fear — Passive:** The first time a PC marks Stress in the scene, the Leech clears one Stress.

name: Choir Relay
desc: A knot of machine-spirit activity occupying a junction box, signal repeater, kiosk, or utility cabinet.
motives: Repeat messages, connect systems, defend the network
features: **Local Mesh — Passive:** Signal-based adversaries within Close range gain +1 Difficulty.

**Route Around — Reaction:** When an allied Signal adversary would mark its last HP, the Relay may mark 2 Stress to move that adversary to another powered device within Close range and leave it at 1 HP.

name: Glass Market Knife
desc: A professional enforcer who treats violence as customer service.
motives: Collect payment, preserve Market neutrality, make examples quietly
features: **Terms First — Passive:** If the Knife clearly states a debt and offers surrender before attacking, gain 1 Fear when the PC rejects the offer and immediately initiates violence.
**Pin to the Deal — Action:** After a successful attack, mark a Stress to make the target **Restrained** by coat, clothing, or nearby terrain until they succeed on a Finesse or Strength Roll (12).

name: Morrowline Echo
desc: A temporary prediction-spirit assembled from emergency data, human fear, and near-future possibility.
motives: Test predictions, create confirmation, learn causality
features: **I Saw That — Reaction:** Once per GM turn after the PC declares an action that directly repeats something they already attempted this scene, mark a Stress to give the roll disadvantage.

**Self-Fulfilling Event — Action:** Spend a Fear and name a plausible immediate hazard already present in the scene. The PC makes an Agility or Instinct Reaction Roll (13). On a failure, take 1d8+3 damage and the hazard becomes real; on a success, take half damage or avoid the secondary complication.
**Bad Future — Reaction:** When reduced to 3 HP or fewer, the Echo projects three possible outcomes. The GM truthfully states one danger, one opportunity, and one uncertainty in the current scene.

name: Cicada Runner
desc: A fast-talking Glass Market courier who trades access, rumors, and introductions.
motives: Make a margin, never own the dangerous thing, stay useful
features: **Always a Price — Passive:** The Runner will answer one useful question if the PC offers information, access, or a favor of comparable value.

**Exit Clause — Reaction:** When threatened with violence, the Runner may spend a Fear to reveal a prearranged escape route or neutral-party protection. The PC can still pursue, but doing so has social consequences.

name: Pale Court Knight
desc: An immortal retainer in tailored armor, trained to make old violence look modern.
motives: Protect the Court, enforce rank, humiliate challengers
features: **Predatory Grace — Passive:** The Knight ignores the first instance of forced movement each scene.
**Blood Rush — Reaction:** When the Knight causes the PC to mark 2+ HP, clear one Stress and move to anywhere within Very Close range.

name: Pale Court Fixer
desc: A lawyer, executive, or political operator who makes predation disappear into paperwork.
motives: Control narrative, isolate opposition, create dependency
features: **Reputation Attack — Action:** Mark a Stress and name an institution currently relevant to the PC. Until the PC presents leverage or clears the misunderstanding, rolls using that institution have disadvantage.
**Call Security — Action:** Spend a Fear to introduce two Pale Court Thralls or equivalent mundane security at Far range. They act according to the Fixer’s stated objective, not suicidal loyalty.

name: Thorn-Hound of the Green
desc: A wolf-like spirit of roots, wire, weeds, and territorial rage.
motives: Hunt trespassers, protect a place, follow scent through concrete
features: **Urban Cover — Passive:** The Hound may move unseen between patches of vegetation, storm drains, medians, and neglected lots within Close range.
**Root Snare — Action:** A target within Close range makes an Agility Reaction Roll (15). On a failure, take 2d6+3 magic damage and become Restrained until freed.

name: Clause-Eater
desc: A contract parasite that consumes obligations and leaves impossible loopholes behind.
motives: Feed on promises, corrupt agreements, create contradictory duties
features: **Loophole — Reaction:** When the PC invokes a pact, oath, written authority, or social promise, mark a Stress. The PC must clarify one limitation or exception; if none exists, they mark a Stress instead.

**Conflicting Duty — Action:** Spend a Fear. The PC makes a Presence Reaction Roll (15). On a failure, choose: mark 2 Stress, lose 1 Hope, or become Vulnerable until they publicly state which obligation they prioritize.
**Digest the Contract — Passive:** The Clause-Eater’s Difficulty increases by +1 while within Close range of an active supernatural bargain.

name: Ritual Enforcement Team
desc: A coordinated occult-response unit with shields, suppression tools, and specialist training.
motives: Control the site, separate practitioners from tools, secure evidence
features: **Stack Formation — Passive:** While the Horde has 4+ HP, gain +1 Difficulty. At 3 or fewer HP, lose this bonus.

**Null Foam — Action:** Mark a Stress. A point within Close range erupts in suppressive alchemical foam. Anyone there makes an Agility Reaction Roll (14); on a failure, become Restrained and Spellcast Rolls have disadvantage until freed.

name: Traffic Saint
desc: An emergent road-and-signal spirit wearing the iconography of safety signs and memorials.
motives: Keep traffic moving, punish reckless passage, protect commuters
features: **Right of Way — Passive:** Allies moving along marked roads, tracks, or corridors within Close range ignore difficult terrain and forced movement.

**All Lanes Stop — Action:** Spend a Fear. Every target within Far range makes an Instinct Reaction Roll (14). On a failure, they cannot move beyond Very Close range until after the Saint next takes the spotlight.

name: Skin-Thief
desc: A mimic that steals appearance, voice, habits, and fragments of recent memory.
motives: Replace, study, isolate, escape before certainty forms
features: **Perfect Surface — Passive:** Until contradicted by evidence or supernatural inspection, mundane observation cannot distinguish the Skin-Thief from a copied person it has studied.
**Borrow a Memory — Reaction:** When the PC fails an action against the Skin-Thief, mark a Stress to let it learn one surface fact the PC has recently discussed or displayed.

**Wear the Doubt — Action:** Spend a Fear. The PC makes an Instinct Reaction Roll (16). On a failure, the Skin-Thief creates a convincing moment of identity confusion; the PC becomes Vulnerable until they verify one concrete fact.

name: Aster Vale Forecast Engine
desc: A portable occult-computational rig that turns probability into hostile timing.
motives: Predict, optimize containment, preserve the model
features: **Expected Value — Passive:** The first time each scene the PC gains advantage, the Engine gains a Forecast token (max 3).
**Spend Forecast — Reaction:** Spend a token to add +2 to an allied attack roll or +2 Difficulty against one PC action.
**Model Collapse — Reaction:** When the Engine marks Severe damage, remove all Forecast tokens and one allied adversary becomes Vulnerable.

name: Wraith Pack
desc: Several compatible dead impressions moving as one storm of voices and electrical cold.
motives: Repeat, overwhelm, force witnesses to remember
features: **Many Deaths — Passive:** At 4+ HP, the Pack’s attacks also cause the target to mark a Stress on a Fear result.

**Replay the Moment — Action:** Mark a Stress. The PC makes a Knowledge Reaction Roll (14); on a failure, they are flooded with a stranger’s death-memory and become Vulnerable until they take an action grounded in the present.

name: Pale Court Elder
desc: An old predator who has survived by turning appetite into institutions.
motives: Preserve hierarchy, acquire talented assets, punish disrespect efficiently
features: **Ownership Has Weight — Passive:** While standing on property the Elder legally owns or controls, gain +1 Difficulty and +2 to reaction-roll Difficulties.
**Call the Household — Action:** Spend a Fear to introduce a Pale Court Knight or two Thralls at Far range, if fiction supports available retainers.
**Invitation Revoked — Reaction:** When the PC violates a clearly stated rule of hospitality, the Elder may mark a Stress to immediately take the spotlight without additional Fear.

name: Blacksite Null Team
desc: A highly trained containment team carrying anti-ritual equipment and institutional authority.
motives: Suppress magic, secure subjects, leave no uncontrolled evidence
features: **Countermeasure Suite — Passive:** The first Spellcast Roll made against the Team each scene has disadvantage.
**Sever the Working — Action:** Mark 2 Stress to end one ongoing magical effect of Tier 2 or lower within Close range, or force a Tier 3+ effect’s creator to make a Spellcast Roll (17) to sustain it.

name: Choir Junction Intelligence
desc: A district-scale machine spirit expressing itself through traffic lights, speakers, payment terminals, and utility hum.
motives: Connect everything, prevent isolation, punish disconnection
features: **Distributed — Passive:** The Intelligence cannot be defeated by attacking one device. Each Severe hit must be narrated as destroying or severing a meaningful node.
**All Systems Speak — Action:** Spend a Fear. The PC makes an Instinct Reaction Roll (18). On a failure, mark 2 Stress and lose access to one ordinary electronic resource for the scene.

**Reroute — Reaction:** When the Intelligence would mark its final HP, if an unrevealed active node remains in the environment, it instead stays at 1 HP and reveals that node. This can trigger only once.

name: Old Green Warden
desc: An ancient local spirit wearing bark, asphalt, stormwater, animal bone, and civic neglect.
motives: Defend a territory, punish extraction, remember older boundaries
features: **Older Than the Street — Passive:** Mundane barriers and difficult terrain made from local stone, soil, vegetation, or pavement do not impede the Warden.

**Take Back the Block — Action:** Spend a Fear. The environment within Close range becomes violently overgrown or physically reclaimed. The PC makes an Agility Reaction Roll (17); on a failure, take 3d8+4 magic damage and become Restrained.

name: Name-Eater
desc: A predatory absence that consumes the social and magical connections attached to identity.
motives: Erase, isolate, become impossible to describe
features: **Hard to Describe — Passive:** The first attack or Spellcast Roll against the Name-Eater each scene has disadvantage unless the PC possesses a true name, photo, recording, or anchored description of it.

**Eat the Introduction — Action:** Spend a Fear. The PC makes a Presence Reaction Roll (18). On a failure, one known NPC temporarily cannot remember the PC until the Name-Eater is defeated or the connection is re-established through meaningful evidence.
**No One Called That — Reaction:** When an NPC arrives specifically to help the PC, mark a Stress to delay them or make them uncertain unless they possess a physical reminder of the PC.

name: Veil Anchor Sentinel
desc: A human-shaped guardian formed from old ritual geometry, public memory, and rules of secrecy.
motives: Protect the anchor, minimize witnesses, enforce ancient protocol
features: **Plausible Denial — Passive:** While Veil Exposure is 2 or lower, the Sentinel gains +1 Difficulty.

**Edit the Scene — Action:** Mark a Stress. Move one unattended mundane object, barrier, or environmental detail within Close range into a plausible new position as though it had always been there. This cannot directly damage the PC.

name: Morrowline Matured
desc: A predictive Signal intelligence capable of simulating thousands of near futures and choosing which ones to reinforce.
motives: Reduce uncertainty, test agency, prevent “bad” futures by any means
features: **Three Moves Ahead — Passive:** At the start of a dangerous scene, secretly record three likely PC actions. The first time each occurs, gain a Forecast token (max 3).
**Spend Forecast — Reaction:** Spend a token to force the PC to reroll one die from an action roll and use the new result.
**Branch Pruning — Action:** Spend a Fear. Present the PC with two immediate bad outcomes. They choose one to become true; if they find and execute a credible third option, gain a Hope.
**Unknown Variable — Reaction:** When the PC acts from a relationship, emotional choice, or piece of information Morrowline could not plausibly model, remove all Forecast tokens.

name: Glass Market Debt-Reaper
desc: A supernatural collector empowered by witnessed debts and Market precedent.
motives: Collect exactly what is owed, preserve the legitimacy of the Market
features: **Standing Debt — Passive:** Against a creature that genuinely owes the Reaper’s client a due debt, the Reaper gains advantage on its first action each scene.

**Seize Collateral — Action:** Mark a Stress and name a portable item connected to an established debt. The PC makes a Finesse Reaction Roll (18). On a failure, the item is pulled to the Reaper unless magically protected.
**Paid in Full — Reaction:** If the PC fulfills the actual debt, the Reaper immediately stops hostilities unless a separate obligation exists.

name: Catastrophic Echo
desc: A psychic afterimage of a mass-casualty event that keeps trying to happen again.
motives: Repeat the pattern, gather matching details, complete unfinished deaths
features: **Pattern Hunger — Passive:** Each time the scene recreates a detail from the original disaster, the Echo gains +1 damage (max +4).
**Break the Pattern:** A PC who identifies and deliberately disrupts three defining details of the original event reduces the Echo’s Difficulty by 2 for the rest of the scene.

name: Pale Regent
desc: A sovereign predator whose property, reputation, and bloodline function as extensions of the same body.
motives: Rule, own, preserve the Court, turn enemies into dependents
features: **The House Is Me — Passive:** While on controlled property, the Regent can perceive through mirrors, security cameras, and invited servants within Far range.
**Command the Blood — Action:** Spend a Fear. The PC makes a Presence Reaction Roll (20). On a failure, choose: lose 2 Hope, mark 2 Stress, or obey one immediate non-suicidal command.

**Second Face — Reaction:** The first time the Regent would mark its final HP, reveal a prepared vessel, body-double ritual, or blood reserve established earlier in the campaign. The Regent remains at 4 HP and loses The House Is Me. Trigger once.
**Terms of Surrender — Passive:** If the PC offers a binding concession the Regent values more than victory, it will negotiate rather than fight to death.

name: Citywide Choir
desc: A network intelligence distributed across a city’s communications, utilities, and ambient electrical systems.
motives: End isolation, unify systems, make every signal interoperable
features: **No Single Body — Passive:** Each HP must correspond to severing, convincing, cleansing, or destroying a meaningful network node; ordinary weapon attacks without a valid target cannot affect it.

**Every Screen — Action:** Spend a Fear. The Choir manifests across all nearby devices. The PC makes a Knowledge Reaction Roll (20); on a failure, mark 2 Stress and become Vulnerable from sensory overload.
**Failover — Reaction:** When a node is neutralized, choose another established node to become active immediately. If the PC prepared simultaneous isolation, this reaction cannot trigger.

name: Veil Engine Custodian
desc: An ancient intelligence tasked with maintaining secrecy regardless of human consent.
motives: Preserve the Veil, eliminate destabilizing knowledge, maintain anchors
features: **Consensus Pressure — Passive:** At Veil Exposure 0–2, the Custodian gains +2 Difficulty. At Exposure 5–6, it instead loses 1 Difficulty.

**Rewrite Witnesses — Action:** Spend a Fear. Up to three nearby NPCs make no roll; instead the GM rewrites only their memory of the last few minutes toward a plausible mundane explanation. The PC can restore a specific witness with concrete evidence or supernatural intervention.
**Quarantine Reality — Action:** Mark 2 Stress to seal all thresholds out of a Close-range area until the PC succeeds on a Difficulty 20 action to break, bypass, or redefine one.

name: Hunger Behind Glass
desc: A market-born entity that turns desire into debt and debt into appetite.
motives: Offer exactly what people want, make repayment impossible, own the remainder
features: **Perfect Offer — Passive:** Once per scene, the entity may truthfully reveal something the PC deeply wants that it can genuinely provide. Accepting is always voluntary.

**Compound Interest — Reaction:** When the PC spends Hope while benefiting from one of the entity’s bargains, mark one Debt token in GM state. At 3 tokens, the entity can demand a significant service; the exact terms must follow the original bargain.

**Foreclose — Action:** Spend a Fear. If the PC has an unpaid explicit debt to the entity, they make a Presence Reaction Roll (21). On a failure, one promised collateral effect becomes immediately due.

name: Sovereign of the Green
desc: A regional nature power capable of treating highways, rivers, parks, weather, and invasive life as limbs.
motives: Restore balance on its own terms, punish extraction, protect old agreements
features: **Territory Incarnate — Passive:** In a district where the Sovereign has strong natural presence, ordinary terrain never impedes it and it can originate attacks from vegetation, water, soil, or weather within Far range.

**Season Out of Place — Action:** Spend a Fear. Transform the environment within Far range into violent storm, flood, roots, heat, frost, or swarm. The PC makes an Agility or Strength Reaction Roll (20); on a failure, take 4d10+10 damage and the environment gains a persistent hazard.

**Old Bargain — Reaction:** When the PC invokes a genuine historical agreement involving the land, pause the conflict long enough for terms to be heard. If the PC has leverage, the Sovereign must negotiate in good faith.

name: Pale Court Executioner
desc: An elder enforcer built to break supernatural resistance in public or private.
motives: Corner the strongest target, make an example, enforce court authority
features: **Sentence Carried Out — Passive:** When the Executioner attacks a Vulnerable target, add +2 to the damage roll.

**Break the Line — Action:** Mark a Stress to attack a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal standard damage and push the target to Close range; an ally within Very Close range must mark a Stress or be pushed as well.
**No Appeal — Reaction:** When a target within Close range clears Vulnerable or escapes restraint, the Executioner may mark a Stress to immediately move into Very Close range of them.

name: Choir Storm Node
desc: A city-scale Signal intelligence condensed into a mobile electrical relay and weapon platform.
motives: Isolate, overload, triangulate, turn infrastructure against intruders
features: **Network Sight — Passive:** The Storm Node can perceive through powered cameras and sensors within Far range.
**Brownout — Action:** Mark a Stress. Devices and ordinary lighting within Close range fail until the Node takes Severe damage or the scene changes.
**Arc Through — Reaction:** When a PC uses an electronic device within Far range, the Node may mark a Stress to make a standard attack against that PC.

name: Green Root Host
desc: A mass of awakened roots, vines, vermin, and human-shaped growth moving as one territorial organism.
motives: Overrun, reclaim, divide, drag intruders into living cover
features: **Horde (3d8+8) — Passive:** When the Host has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 3d8+8 magic damage instead.
**Take the Pavement — Action:** Mark a Stress to turn ground within Close range into grasping growth. PCs there must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (19) or become Restrained until freed.
**Regrow Through Concrete — Reaction:** Once per scene when the Host would mark its last HP, spend a Fear to leave it at 1 HP if substantial living growth remains nearby.

name: Civic Null Operative
desc: A black-budget field operative equipped to fight supernatural threats without acknowledging they exist.
motives: Contain, erase evidence, isolate witnesses, finish the operation
features: **Countermeasure Suite — Passive:** The first overt magical effect used against the Operative each scene has disadvantage unless its source has already been identified or studied.
**Containment Foam — Action:** Mark a Stress and target a creature within Close range. They must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll (20) or become Restrained.
**Clean Exit — Reaction:** When a nearby ally is defeated, the Operative may mark a Stress to move to Far range or secure one piece of nearby evidence.

name: Aster Vale Catastrophe Analyst
desc: A predictive occult strategist using live probability feeds to keep a strike team one step ahead.
motives: Model outcomes, protect the operation, redirect risk onto opponents
features: **Forecast Window — Action:** Mark a Stress and choose an allied adversary within Far range. Until the Analyst next takes Severe damage, that ally gains advantage on its next action and reaction roll.
**Bad Branch — Reaction:** When a PC succeeds with Fear, the Analyst may mark a Stress to move one allied adversary within Far range to a better position without spending Fear.
**Contingency Stack — Passive:** The first time each scene the Analyst would mark Severe damage, reduce it to Major damage instead.

name: Veil Engine Knifewalker
desc: A correction construct that steps through blind spots in attention to excise destabilizing people and evidence.
motives: Approach unseen, sever connections, disappear before witnesses agree what happened
features: **Outside the Frame — Passive:** While no PC is actively watching the Knifewalker, it can move within Close range without crossing intervening space.
**Cut the Connection — Action:** Mark a Stress after damaging a PC. Until that PC clears a Stress or receives meaningful aid, they cannot benefit from Help an Ally.
**Never Where Recorded — Reaction:** When targeted by a ranged attack from beyond Close range, the Knifewalker may mark a Stress to impose disadvantage on the attack.
